newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 10.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:

* The first commercial spy satellite is scheduled to be launched in April or May, with others to follow, giving anyone with a credit card access to information previously obtainable only by the governments of advanced nations. Among the companies involved are Eastman Kodak, Earthwatch -- whose partners include a unit of Ball Corp and Hitachi Ltd -- and Space Imaging Inc, a private company owned by Lockheed Martin and Raytheon's E-Systems Inc.

* Law enforcement officials say Mafia families in the northeast are switching increasingly to white-collar crimes, focusing on fraud, particularly in the areas of health insurance, pre-paid telephone calls and small Wall Street brokerages.

* Interviews with U.S. Army officials and female recruits, a review of the Pentagon's surveys on sexual harassment and an examination of cases show that recent charges of sex abuse within the Army are not isolated incidents, but problems whose roots date as far back as two decades.
* The Ecuadoran presidency crises ended peacefully on Sunday after an agreement was reached for Vice-President Rosalia Arteaga to serve as interim president.
* New York hospitals began the open mandatory testing of newborns for HIV this month in the first such programme in the nation.

* After many years in which torture was incorporated into its justice system, Cambodia is beginning to develop a small corps of lawyers and judges to train its police officers in proper procedures and to revive the rudiments of a legal system.

* Michael Forbes says he is constantly snubbed in the halls of Congress as one of five Republicans who voted against Republican Speaker Newt Gingrich after Gingrich admitted providing inaccurate information to a House ethics committee investigating his use of tax-exempt funds for political activities.
